flags.why: Calling people an evil master's henchmen is derogatory, and this sense lacks a warning tag.
Ngày mùng một means the first day of a lunar month here, without specifying the first day of the year.
flags.fix: She is very superstitious and does not dare sweep the house on the first day of the lunar month.

flags.why: The entry omits the common insulting use meaning a contemptible or worthless person, illustrated in this [published novel](https://fliphtml5.com/oimsx/fbza/V%E1%BA%BFt_Th%C3%B9_H%E1%BA%B1n_Tr%C3%AAn_L%C6%B0ng_Ng%E1%BB%B1a_Hoang/91/).
flags.fix: Add a sense tagged derogatory, offensive: a contemptible or worthless person.

flags.why: The example explains the word rather than using it to refer to an areca palm.
flags.fix: Trước sân có một hàng nang. = There is a row of areca palms in front of the house.

flags.why: The entry omits the common noun meaning mud or mire, recorded in the [dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-b%C3%B9n%20l%E1%BA%A7y).

This sense occurs in ordinary speech about crowds or work diminishing and is not restricted to literary language, as the [dictionary examples](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-v%C3%A3n) show.
The entry omits the common verb meaning to imply, which is recorded separately in the [dictionary](https://loigiaihay.com/tu-dien-tv/ham-y-e4KRK3piNW3X1.html).
